title: Biography: Who I Am
text: Biography: Who I Am. My name is Hafsa. I am 21 years old. I was born in Sohar, Oman, but I grew up in Sialkot, Punjab, Pakistan, a city best known for its sports goods and surgical instruments. I am the middle child of three siblings, which comes with its own set of middle-child syndrome and behaviours. Growing up between an older and a younger sibling has shaped my personality in ways that are sometimes difficult to explain. At home, we speak Punjabi and Urdu, while my education has been in English, so I naturally switch between three languages in my daily life. Childhood. As a child, I was a very joyful, playful, and somewhat childish kid. I was an average student who never seemed particularly concerned about studies, yet somehow managed to secure a position in class. Studying was never really my biggest priority, but things usually worked out academically. My interest in computers developed differently than most people's. Instead of being fascinated by programming or technology from the beginning, I became curious about computers through stories and discussions about hacking. The idea that someone could explore systems, discover hidden vulnerabilities, and understand how technology works behind the scenes caught my attention. That curiosity gradually developed into an interest in computer science and cybersecurity. Turning Points. One important thing about my journey is that becoming a doctor was never my dream.

text: The idea that someone could explore systems, discover hidden vulnerabilities, and understand how technology works behind the scenes caught my attention. That curiosity gradually developed into an interest in computer science and cybersecurity. Turning Points. One important thing about my journey is that becoming a doctor was never my dream. It was not something I wanted for myself, and neither did my parents expect me to become one. Similarly, becoming a government officer was never a goal for me or something my parents envisioned for my future. Choosing my own direction and pursuing computer science was a natural decision rather than an attempt to follow someone else's expectations. I wanted to explore something that genuinely interested me, and technology gave me that opportunity. My growing curiosity about hacking and cybersecurity eventually helped shape the direction I wanted to take. Where I Am Now. Today, I live in Sialkot, Pakistan, study Computer Science at university, and work full-time in software quality assurance. I am not a morning person; I would much rather enjoy a little extra sleep than wake up early without a good reason. I consider myself an introvert who genuinely enjoys being alone. I am not particularly fond of socializing or being surrounded by people all the time. I value my personal space, enjoy my own company, and prefer keeping my thoughts and personal matters to myself rather than sharing everything with others.

title: Education: School, College and University
text: Education: School, College and University. School. I completed my matriculation at Harvard Grammar High School in 2021, scoring 1,079 out of 1,100 marks. I was a good student academically, although I never had a particular favourite subject except Computer Science. I was never interested in activities like debates or public speaking, as those things were not really my type of thing. However, I served as a school proctor, which gave me the opportunity to develop communication, responsibility, and leadership skills. It also helped me learn how to interact with different people and handle responsibilities. College. I completed my FSc in Pre-Engineering at Punjab College from 2021 to 2023. Since I chose Pre-Engineering, I did not get the opportunity to study computers or programming during this period. My academic focus was mainly on subjects like mathematics, physics, and chemistry. Although I did not have a formal background in computer science before university, I eventually developed my interest in technology and started learning about computers when I began my bachelor's degree. University. I started my BS in Computer Science at UMT in 2023. I have completed six semesters so far and am currently progressing through my final year. University has been quite a challenging experience academically. I would not describe myself as a top student or someone who always finds studying easy. I consider myself an average student who has managed to get through difficult courses, sometimes with a lot of struggle, frustration, and even tears. However, not every course was equally difficult or uninteresting. title: My Opinions and Hot Takes
text: My Opinions and Hot Takes. On Technology. I believe technology is much more interesting when you understand what happens behind the screen. I am particularly interested in cybersecurity and penetration testing because I find it fascinating how systems can be explored, tested, and sometimes exploited through vulnerabilities. I also believe that security should not be treated as an optional feature. Developers should think about potential security risks while building applications rather than waiting until something goes wrong. On Artificial Intelligence. I think artificial intelligence is a powerful tool, but it should not replace human thinking. It can make learning easier, explain complicated concepts, and help people work more efficiently, but blindly depending on it can limit our ability to solve problems independently. I believe AI should be used as an assistant, not as a substitute for understanding. On Education. I believe academic grades do not always reflect someone's actual abilities. title: My Projects and Research
text: My Projects and Research. This document describes some of the academic, research and software projects I have worked on or developed as proposals. It includes their objectives, technologies, technical approaches and the problems they aim to solve. 1. SentinelEdge. Project Overview. SentinelEdge is a conceptual research proposal focused on developing a Byzantine-resilient Federated Learning framework for intrusion detection in MQTT-based Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial Control Systems (ICS). The primary motivation behind this research is to improve intrusion detection while preserving the privacy of distributed IoT devices. Instead of requiring all devices to share their raw data with a central server, Federated Learning allows participants to train models collaboratively. Problem Statement. Traditional centralized intrusion detection systems may require collecting data from multiple devices at a central location. This creates privacy concerns and can introduce security vulnerabilities. Federated Learning helps address the data-sharing problem, but malicious or compromised participants can send manipulated model updates that affect the global model. SentinelEdge proposes a Byzantine-resilient approach to address this challenge. Targeted Attacks. The research focuses on four attack categories: Reconnaissance Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) Replay attacks Zero-day attacks Proposed Technical Architecture. The proposed framework explores multiple detection and defense components: Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) for reconnaissance detection. CNN-BiLSTM for MitM attack detection. Transformer-based detection for replay attacks. Federated learning using the Flower framework. FedProx for federated model optimization. Additional defenses against malicious model updates. The research also explores privacy-preserving mechanisms such as Differential Privacy and Secure Aggregation. Research Status. SentinelEdge is a conceptual research proposal presented at ICARMP 2026 at UMT Lahore. The work was presented in the conference poster category. The proposed architecture and methodology were developed as research concepts. The framework had not yet undergone full implementation or experimental evaluation at the time of presentation.
